clue.text: Tell Lucy: coin minted for local authority

parts.note: to tell is an old sense of to count, as in a bank teller or telling beads

indicators.note: coins are minted by being stamped out of raw metal, so the letters are recast into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to inform Lucy that a coin has been struck for the town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like an instruction to speak to Lucy, but it is a verb meaning count; only Lucy and coin are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a county council is the elected body that governs a county, a standard tier of local government.

clue.text: Radical university, a part of London

parts.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary radical
the London School of Economics, a university college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A district of London is home to a politically radical university.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface but is just a letter in the wordplay. The LSE is a famous London university, known for left-wing students.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a wealthy district in west London, beside the Thames, so it is one named part of the capital.

clue.text: A little rum (a mild taste)

indicators.note: only a small portion of the words that follow is taken, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the letters run across these words, ignoring the bracket

explanation.surface: A small sip of rum gives a gentle flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the join between the words; the answer sits across the end of rum and the start of 'a mild'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter, named from Japanese.

clue.text: Record: wine gradually diminished

parts.note: to record something is to tape it
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: A record of wine sales shows them slowly falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' is a verb here, not a noun such as a disc or ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tapered became steadily narrower or smaller, like a candle or a dwindling supply.

clue.text: Bent copper, crime etc: I activated measure

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: set in motion, these letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman's crimes set off some official measure against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent copper' reads as a crooked policeman, but copper is the chemical element and bent joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubic centimetre is a unit of volume, so it is a measure in the sense of a standard unit.

clue.text: One solver honoured in announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so what matters is how the words are heard

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you, and someone honoured by the monarch is knighted

explanation.surface: A crossword solver is publicly named in an honours announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'you knighted' runs into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are one are joined together in agreement, the same sense as 'we stand as one'.

clue.text: One creche assembled union

indicators.note: putting parts together into a new whole means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nursery is put together by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is the definition in the sense of things holding together.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of parts sticking together as a consistent whole, a close synonym for unity.

clue.text: Relaxed dipping into Milan guidebook

indicators.note: dipping into something reaches inside it, so the letters are found within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A tourist idly browses a guidebook to Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the city name and the start of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid describes someone slow, lazy and unhurried in movement, a close synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: A lovely person's back? Very good

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a gem is a lovely person

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lovely person's back as very good.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive looks like part of the surface, but 's back is read as 'is back', the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for excellent or great, so it praises something as very good.

clue.text: Running tavern, taking time writing menu including starter of haggis

parts.note: a pub is a tavern

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one piece goes inside another
to take something away is to remove it, so a letter goes

parts.note: writing a menu is listing the dishes
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of haggis

explanation.surface: Someone runs a pub and takes time writing up a menu that features haggis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like it describes the pub, but it is the definition, as in running a newspaper. One T comes out of the menu word, and the haggis letter fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a magazine or paper means producing and issuing it, which is what publishing does.

clue.text: Losing cent, clerk increasingly pale

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a cashier is a bank or shop clerk
C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: A clerk who keeps losing money grows paler with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: The cent is a single letter removed from the front of the clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means grey and pallid like ash, so the comparative form describes a face becoming more pale.

clue.text: Opening of Coriolanus, tragedy needing excision: that's obvious

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Coriolanus
King Lear, Shakespeare's tragedy
an excision is a cut

explanation.surface: The start of Coriolanus needs trimming, as any director can see.
explanation.walkthrough: Coriolanus sets up a Shakespeare theme, but it only gives one letter; the tragedy is a different play.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear-cut case is plain and unambiguous, so the hyphenated adjective is a synonym for obvious.

clue.text: Found fault with Independent writer about Latin expression

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
I is the abbreviation for independent

indicators.note: turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone criticised a writer for The Independent newspaper over a Latin phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' and 'writer' suggest a journalist at the newspaper, but they give a single letter and the setter's word for themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is a Latin motto from Horace, usually rendered 'seize the day'.

clue.text: Musician's press release to approve disc by Furious Five

parts.note: PR is public relations, the business of press releases

indicators.note: something in a fury is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it
the letter O is round like a disc
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band's publicist announces approval of a record by a group called the Furious Five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furious Five' reads as a band name, but the first word is the shuffling signal for the number written out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev was a Russian composer, of Peter and the Wolf among other works, so he is a musician.

clue.text: Tennyson heroine to eat in style after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A Tennyson heroine dines elegantly once she has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving a job or going to bed; here it means drawing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is the faithful wife of Geraint in Tennyson's Idylls of the King, a poem cycle about Arthurian knights.

clue.text: Component of servo (Boeing instrument)

indicators.note: a component is one part inside a larger thing, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the bracket

explanation.surface: A part of a servomechanism forms one of the instruments of a Boeing aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a cockpit gauge in the aircraft setting, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind of the orchestra, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Big cocaine bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken apart, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Police make a huge drugs seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' is a police raid in the surface and the signal for rearranging letters in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic can mean vast, as huge as an ocean, so it serves as an adjective for very large.

clue.text: Arranged systematically; shocked!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: set out at regular intervals, like shifts or start times

explanation.walkthrough: The semicolon separates two unrelated meanings of the same past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered hours are spread out in an orderly pattern, while being staggered by news means being astonished or amazed.

clue.text: German Enigma that's set on fire

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
an enigma is a riddle

explanation.surface: A German Enigma coding machine is deliberately burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German Enigma' suggests the wartime cipher machine, but it splits into a letter and a word for a puzzle. 'Set on fire' means placed over the flame, not burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron cooking plate placed over a flame or hob to heat.

clue.text: In brasserie, at the end, old trick: Everyman's saving money

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of brasserie
a con is a trick or swindle
O is the abbreviation for old
the setter Everyman would say my for his own

explanation.surface: At the end of a brasserie meal, the diner pulls an old trick to save cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Everyman's' means 'belonging to me'. The trick precedes the old letter in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy is careful use of money and resources, so it is the act of saving rather than spending.

clue.text: Live, accepting love — and prosper

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to dwell somewhere is to live there
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A play on the Vulcan blessing 'Live long and prosper', with love added.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Mr Spock's Star Trek greeting, which tempts a solver to read 'Live' as part of a quotation rather than a verb meaning reside.
explanation.definitionFit: To do well is to succeed or thrive, a plain idiom meaning the same as to prosper.

clue.text: Primarily jumbo epicurean receptacle: outsize bottle of aerated merriment!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.words: jumbo epicurean receptacle: outsize bottle of aerated merriment
parts.note: the first letters of the eight words

explanation.surface: A gourmet's enormous vessel full of bubbly party spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue after the indicator describes the answer, while its initials spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large champagne bottle holding four standard bottles, and champagne is the fizzy drink of celebration.

clue.text: Foremost of Inuit gaffs with small rooms?

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
a loo is a small room, the toilet

explanation.surface: Inuit homes are imagined with tiny lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaff is British slang for someone's home. The two words supply both the initials and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Igloos are the traditional snow-block dwellings of the Inuit, so they are Inuit homes.

clue.text: Left without 100 goods' slow movement

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: cargo is goods carried by a ship or plane
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred goods were left behind and are slow to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' sounds like sluggish freight, but it is a musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a tempo marking for very slow, broad playing, and a symphony movement may be named after it.

clue.text: Grub: for starters, one in France gets 'minced steed' — not eaten

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: mincing chops something into small pieces, so the letters are cut up and remixed

parts.note: to grub is to dig in the soil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner in France is served minced horse as a starter and leaves it untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food, fitting the dinner scene, but it is the verb meaning dig; 'for starters' puts the French word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left undigested has not been broken down by the stomach, loosely matching food not eaten.

clue.text: Loudly regretted getting cross

indicators.note: saying something loudly means it is heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone loudly regrets losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry in the surface, but it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially the large one above a church screen, so it is a cross.

clue.text: 104 come in with lyre playing for declaration of love

parts.note: 104 in Roman numerals is C (100) plus IV (4)

indicators.note: playing with things moves them about freely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hundred and four musicians arrive strumming lyres to serenade a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The number looks like a crowd of people, but it is read as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil ceremony is a non-religious wedding, at which a couple formally pledge themselves to each other.
